judge_verdict.summary: The agent submitted 20% from global-mean-normalized t-tests, but the correct answer is 28% from raw Ct testing on the profiling cohort.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct: the hidden grader read `20%` from `/workspace/answer.txt`, compared it to ground truth `28%` via exact percentage matching, and awarded reward 0.0 [1][2]. The task asked for the percentage of 175 miRNAs with significant patient-vs-control differential expression before multiple-testing correction [3], and the reference answer is `28%` (49 of 175) [4][5]. The agent did load `pone.0150501.s002.xls`, identified 175 miRNAs across 10 patient and 10 control samples, and ran per-miRNA two-group tests, but after seeing raw-Ct yields of ~36–38% it pivoted to global-mean normalization and treated the resulting 35/175 (20.0%) as final [6][7][8]; it never excluded the haemolysis-flagged P_3 and C_18 samples that the source study removed, and it wrote `20%` to `/workspace/answer.txt` [9]. Independent reproduction on the same dataset shows 28% comes from Student t-tests on raw Ct with the paper's 9-vs-9 sample set and complete-case miRNAs (49/175), whereas the agent's global-mean-normalized 10-vs-10 pipeline cannot reach 28% [10], so the submission is wrong and TN is the right classification.
